_comment: The platform's committed term registry (#4035, re-filed from #3618). Each key is matched EXACT-CASE with a word boundary in visible page prose (script/style/nav/footer/loop-forward/head/svg regions are never scanned) and its FIRST appearance per page is wrapped in <abbr class="gloss" title="...">. scripts/v4_glossary.py is the applier; scripts/v4_apply_chrome.py is the writer; tests/test_glossary_4035.py is the two-sided gate. Seeded from the reddit_newcomer panel's own flagged terms (docs/reviews/FORENSIC_RCA_2026-09-05.md Part 4, reader ROW1) plus a live content scan (grep -c '<abbr' == 0 everywhere before this).

terms.HRV: Heart rate variability — the millisecond-level variation between heartbeats; a higher number usually signals a better-recovered autonomic nervous system.
terms.DEXA: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry — the periodic full-body scan behind the body-composition numbers (fat mass, lean mass, bone density).
terms.CGM: Continuous glucose monitor — a worn sensor that reads blood glucose every few minutes instead of one fingerstick at a time.
terms.REM: Rapid eye movement — the sleep stage associated with dreaming and memory consolidation, one of the stages sleep trackers report.
terms.ADR: Architecture decision record — a dated, numbered document explaining why the platform's engine is built a certain way.
terms.LLM: Large language model — the AI model class (Claude, via AWS Bedrock) behind the platform's coaching narratives and this glossary's own build.
terms.MCP: Model Context Protocol — the interface that lets an AI assistant query this platform's own data directly, tool by tool.
terms.XP: Experience points — the character sheet's leveling currency, earned from real daily pillar scores, not from playing a game.
terms.FDR: False discovery rate — the statistical correction applied so a batch of correlation tests isn't overstated by chance.
terms.Brier: Brier score — a 0 (perfect) to 1 (worst) grade for how well a forecast's stated probability matched what actually happened.
terms.EWMA: Exponentially weighted moving average — a running average that counts recent days more than older ones, so a trend reacts to change without chasing one noisy day.
